title: A `user` reference that resolves to nothing renders as a plain person's name in record detail, while the edit form shows it empty — read and write give opposite answers about the same value
body:
Routed from **objectstack-ai/cloud#2074** by the `repo:cloud` PM seat; drafted by the dev seat that investigated it. ⚠️ **The read-path analysis below was taken from source in this repo but was NOT executed** — no rig, no browser. Re-measure before acting.

⚠️ **This card needs objectui triage** (`domain:*` + a `pm:*` state). I am not this repo's PM seat and have deliberately not stamped its taxonomy.

## What the user sees

When a `type: 'user'` field holds an unresolvable bare string (e.g. a person's name written into the column), the **same value** gets three different answers:

| surface | shows |
|---|---|
| record detail | plain text — the name, **no avatar** — indistinguishable from a filled text field |
| edit form | picker is **blank** ("Select…"), yet it submits that invisible original value |
| save | refused by reference validation: `reference_not_found` |

The read side says "there is a person here", the write side says "there is nothing here", and the truth is "there is an invalid reference here". None of the three answers is that.

## Root cause (source-level, located — ⚠️ not executed)

`packages/fields/src/index.tsx`, `UserCellRenderer` (~line 2067), first branch:

```
// Primitive value: just display the ID/username as text
if (typeof value !== 'object') {
  return TruncatedText(text = String(value));   // JSX elided
}
```

When the reference **resolves**, the value arrives as an object (`{ name, image, … }`) and renders as avatar + name. When it **fails to resolve**, expand produces no object, the value is still the raw string, and it falls into this primitive branch and is printed as if it were an "ID/username".

⭐ **The problem is the branch's premise.** The comment says it is displaying "the ID or username" — but on a `user` field, a primitive arriving here means precisely that **expand did not resolve it**. Printing it as a displayable identity renders "resolution failed" as "resolution succeeded". The missing avatar is the only difference, and that is a **subtractive** signal (something absent), not an **additive** one (a stated warning). Nothing anywhere says the reference is invalid.

## Suggested direction (⛔ implementation not presumed)

At minimum, record detail should render an unresolved reference **as unresolved** rather than impersonating a real person. Two strengths:

1. **Weak** — keep the raw value but mark it unresolved (dimmed / a "not found" affordance / a tooltip), so a human can tell it is not a normal name.
2. **Strong** — make read and write agree: the edit form already treats it as empty; render detail by the same test instead of the two disagreeing.

⚠️ **Do NOT close this by making the renderer tolerate the bad value more gracefully.** cloud's AGENTS.md "contract-first" section forbids absorbing bad metadata at the consumer. This card asks for **honest display**, not tolerance.

## Boundaries

- **The producer side is already fixed in cloud** (cloud#2074 / cloud PR #2083, squash `eadb3446`): new seeds no longer write person names into `user` columns.
- **Existing rows are unchanged**, and hand-authored metadata, installed packages, or any future generator can still produce the same value — so honest rendering does not become unnecessary because the producer was fixed.
- **The save refusal is correct** (fail-closed) — ⛔ do not loosen it. This card is about **display** only.

## Evidence limit, stated plainly

The read path was read in source; the **edit-form blank behaviour was inferred** from `LookupField` delegation and was **not** reproduced. The original reporter observed the blank form directly in a browser; the dev seat that wrote this analysis did not.

Origin: objectstack-ai/cloud#2074.
